messages:
sam-sales: Quick sync 1 LargeCorp procurement wants an on-prem air-gapped POC. Requirements: signed incremental patches, no outbound network during install, explicit key delivery (they prefer sneakernet), and documented rollback pathway. Need quick answers for the commercial response.

tara-solutions: OK. Two primary signing flows: 1) Customer-managed keys: they hold the private key (HSM/USB), we sign locally or they sign and we verify. 2) Redwood-signed bundles with attestation logs. Which do they prefer?

mike-eng: Minibundles (delta-friendly) are our recommended path for on-prem. Format: chunked tar.gz + manifest + bundle.sha256. We sign manifest with Notary v2 by default. For customer signing, we can produce unsigned manifests for them to sign on-site.

jen-security: Security constraints: We support customer HSM/KMS. If they want FIPS-validated flows and yearly rotation, note extra paperwork and attestation. One-liner for questionnaire: "Yes 1 Redwood supports customer-managed signing keys (HSM/KMS) for offline bundle signing; see attached key-injection and attestation runbook."

ops-engr: On the transfer side: recommend AES-256 encrypted minibundles with envelope key delivered on a sealed USB. Transfer tip: use `rsync --partial --inplace` and verify with `sha256sum -c bundle.sha256` and `./verify-manifest --pubkey /opt/keys/bank.pub bundle.manifest.sig`. We include a local-only apply script.

tara-solutions: Upgrade cadence question: propose quarterly deltas (4/year) plus emergency hotfix SLA (48h for critical). Pricing lines: POC eng (2 wks) $32k; signed-bundle subscription $24k/year for 4 deltas + verification support; customer HSM integration $7k one-time. Confirm?

sam-sales: That looks fine. Procurement also asked whether offline artifacts contain any telemetry or phoning-home. We need a definitive statement.

mike-eng: Definitive: Offline bundles contain no outbound telemetry. We strip monitoring endpoints, disable telemetry flags, and only leave a local apply log file. No network calls during install or post-install by default.

jen-security: Addendum: we can provide an enterprise attestation packet (bundle signature chain + signing certificate) as part of the delivery to satisfy compliance reviewers.

tara-solutions: For the SOW I'll include the option for encrypted minibundles. If they choose encrypted at-rest, we need to know if they want the envelope key handed over via sneakernet (USB) or KMS-wrapped envelope. If sneakernet, we provide the runbook for key-injection.

sam-sales: Procurement also worried about rollback. Can you confirm rollback steps look safe (re-apply previous minibundle)?

mike-eng: Rollback = re-apply previous signed minibundle; the operator enforces manifest version checks and aborts if preconditions fail. We'll include a preflight check: `./verify-manifest --check-compat` and a rollback validation script.

ops-engr: I'll draft a short runbook snippet with commands and a checklist: checksum verify, decompress, run preflight, apply, post-boot verify. Also include resume strategy if transfer interrupted.

tara-solutions: Sophie, can you provide the one-liner for the security questionnaire now?

jen-security: One-liner: "Yes. Redwood supports customer-managed signing keys (HSM/KMS) for offline bundle signing and can operate with customer-held keys or provide HSM-backed signing with attestation; see attached runbook."

sam-sales: Great. @ticket-bot please open a POC request for LargeCorp with tags: airgap, sneakernet, customer-hsm, quarterly-patches. Include the proposed pricing lines and runbook draft as attachments.

ticket-bot: POC created: LC-POC-2026-301. Assigned to mike-eng. ETA initial artifact: 6 business days.

sam-sales: Thanks everyone. I'll add these answers to the commercial response and security questionnaire and flag the HSM pricing as optional. If procurement pushes for live key escrow we'll need legal input. Closing thread for now. :thumbsup:
